description: Oyez! Oyez! His most Mighty and Noble Excellency Muireadhach Ã CuileannÃ¡in, Baron of Buckland Cross, has sworn to perform a great feat of nobility and prowess. He, along with several other noble warriors of the Southern region, have made a vow to hold the field in that same barony on the sixth day of June, against any who would meet them. All who would witness the clash of arms and who would mark great moments of prowess, should gather there for a pleasant diversion of glory and violence. Any who would stand as venans must present themselves, armed cap a pied, but with helmet in hand, to the marshals, the heralds, the King at Arms, and the ministers of the lists, which shall be built on the common for this occasion, at 11 of the clock on the day appointed. Bear on your body a surcotte of your arms, and display any banner or pennon to which your rank entitles you. Then issue your challenge to the tenans, that they may give you your desire. Any who would witness these hectors and hercules in their feats of arms, who would cheer their bravery, or who has a champion who shall bear some token of thine in the lists, should gather at that same place and time. For glory, honor, and chivalry! Long reign the Crown! ********** The Emprise of the Red Stag is a pas dâ'armes in the tradition of King Renee, combined with a ransom tourney in the tradition of The Greatest Tournament, the Combat of the 30, William Marshal tourneys, and the Deed at GNEW. The format shall be as follows: There shall be a King of Arms to act as marshal, see that the rules of the deed and the rules of the lists are followed, pursuant to the rules and regulations of the East Kingdom. All decisions of the King of Arms shall be final. First Round The first round shall be a challenge round, where the tenens, captained by the Baron of Buckland Cross, shall accept challenges from all comers. A tree of battle with four shields shall be set up next to the barrier. Each of the venans shall stand forth, with their herald if they have one, announce themselves, and issue their challenge by striking one of the four shields: * Red: for combat to first blood (under SCA rules) * Blue: for counted blows landed, 3, 5, or 7 * Yellow: for a three-man melee combat (targets and blows to be negotiated) * Black: for a timed 60 second combat The challenger shall state what weapons they will use, if the combat is to be upon the field or at the barrier, and whether or not the targets are limited to between the quarters or if limbs also count. Each of the tenans may only be challenged once, until all have been challenged. Then, they will be challenged again, until all the venans have issued their challenges. The following rules apply to this round: * There are no shields allowed at the barrier. * Basket hilted weapons are allowed. * All blows must be struck above the top rail of the barrier * Thrusting is only allowed with six foot spears * No unpadded polearms (6 foot unpadded polearms may be used as spears) * When fighting with a single-handed weapon at the barrier, in a combat between only two combatants, each combatant must grasp the top rail of the barrier with their free hand,. If they let go of the barrier, they forfeit. Second Round The second round of the tournament shall be a ransom tournament consisting of two even teams lasting 30 minutes. The following rules apply to this round: * Each fighter must bring tokens, commensurate with their estate, with which to pay ransoms * The tenans shall enter from one side of the field, the venans from the other. These sides of the field represent their safe zones, where prisoners must brought to be ransomed * All blows are to be between the quarters (limbs donât count) * There are no killing blows * A fighter is captured when struck a good blow in the head or torso, or a good thrust * Thrusts only count to the arm pits, or to the face of an open-faced helmet * Captured fighters must accompany their captors off the field * Fighters may be rescued only if their captor is struck and captured themselves * Captured fighters may not run, yell, try to escape, or resist leaving the field in any way. If an attempt is made to rescue them they must await the outcome of the attempt and act accordingly * A rescued fighter must accompany their rescuer and former captor off the field, and then re-enter at the appropriate side * Once ransomed, prisoners must return to their original side of the field * If a fighter wishes to re-enter the field after being ransomed, they must enter from their original side of the field * Fighters are requested to make an attempt at 14th or 15th century armor but for this year's event, it is not required * No basket hilts allowed â cross hilts only * No weapons more than six feet allowed * No thrusting allowed with single-handed weapons * No unpadded polearms (except the ones 6 feet long being used as spears) * No exposed plastic armor The combat shall be timed, and proceed for a half hour, not counting holds. Ransoms must be settled at the end of the combat. Third Round The third round shall be a timed single stick relay at the barrier. Basket hilts are allowed. Final Round/Prizes The last round shall be the final challenge. The venans shall choose from amongst themselves the fighter they believe showed the greatest nobility on the day, and he shall challenge any of the tenans for the honor of the dayâs final combat. This is the venans prize. * Each of the tenans shall give a token to a fighter they believe showed great courage, prowess, nobility, or courtesy * There shall be a prize awarded by the gallery * There shall be a prize awarded by the King of Arms * All combatants, both tenans and venans, are eligible for these last two prizes ****Not fighting? Join the gallery!**** Every tournament needs an audience to witness heroic deeds and cheer on their favorites! The gallery welcomes all to an immersive experience transporting you to the fourteenth century. We will have music, food, and an atmosphere to rival the grandest tourney! Members of the gallery will have the opportunity the fighter whom captured their heart and bestow upon a prize (made by Magnifica Scolastica). Members of the gallery are encouraged to wear 14th century dress, feast gear, and bring period appropriate seating (or camouflage modern items) to make this immersive experience possible. description: Our theme for this year will be the sentiment "We have always been here". We heartily encourage the incorporation of PRIDE colors (Rainbow or the Pride flag of your choice) with your pageantry. From the PrideFEST page: “Middletown PrideFEST is the State of Connecticut’s largest pride event held in downtown Middletown, Connecticut, on the first Saturday of June (6/6). PrideFEST starts at 12 pm and ends at 10 pm. PrideFEST is an all-afternoon street festival that includes family friendly fun and activities for all ages. PrideFEST consists of the Middletown Pride March, Pride Rally, Pride Showcase Concert, and a Tea Dance. Vendors and food trucks will be located on Main Street. Don’t forget to stop by the Middletown Pride Merchandise Tent to purchase your exclusive Middletown Pride swag, sign up for our newsletter, and learn about what we do all year. PrideFEST draws over 35,000 individuals, 130 vendors, and 80 marching groups from all over New England to downtown Middletown.” It is recommended to arrive at the event early as parking will likely be abysmal due to the number of overall attendees. There is typically a large parking lot available off Dingwall Street just off of Main Street. Early arrivers can join us in Union Park at the south end of Main Street. The march starts at the north end of Main Street (about a ¾ mile walk) on PEASE AVE between North St. and Stack St. Plan to be at the parade start point between 12-12:30. The parade will commence at 1 PM. The parade ends at Union Park. The entire site is outdoors. The park has paved walkways and handicap ramps at most intersections. We acknowledge that some people may have concerns for personal safety, and we agree that your safety is paramount. We can say from our experiences of the 2024 and 2025 events, that the local Middletown Police, Emergency Services, and Fire Departments are ALL very supportive of this event and maintain a positive, high profile at this event. The vendors and attendees are wonderful. This should be an amazing day! The weather can be mercurial, so plan to bring some covering in case of rain. We hope that it will be a beautiful day so that we can showcase all the amazing pageantry that makes the Society the amazing experience that it is. Step out in your spiffiest kit, bring your personal arms and banners for display and plan to have a wonderful day. Please plan to bring your own food and drinks as needed. There are many food and drink vendors available for purchase (as well as a wide variety of restaurants in downtown Middletown). IMPORTANT NOTES: Consider this a DRY site. description: Come join us at Carolingian Dance Practice! The winter/spring 2026 practices will be on fourth Tuesdays: Feb 24, Mar 24, Apr 28, May 26, and June 23rd. This is a fun social occasion for all: an evening where we all get together to learn Renaissance Dances and socialize with the members of the Barony. It is specifically newcomer-friendly: all dances are taught, you don’t need to come with a partner (we encourage folks to switch partners from dance to dance), and folks generally come in street clothes. Just wear something comfortable that you can move in (especially comfortable shoes). We meet from 7:30 – 9:30pm at the Holy Trinity Armenian Church, at 145 Brattle Street in Cambridge. There’s a parking lot for those who need to drive, bus routes nearby, and it’s less than a 20 minute walk from the Harvard Square MBTA station. The parking lot is off of Sparks Street, on the far side of the Church away from Brattle Street. (If using a GPS, 62 Sparks Street is roughly across the street from the parking lot.) The hall where we will be dancing is next to the parking lot, so if you are walking up Brattle Street, turn onto Sparks Street to get to the hall. If the front door on Sparks Street is locked, come around to the parking lot side and use the door there. Dances are taught and called using the gender-free “Larks and Robins” style, popular with many of the local dance communities. We have a lot of space (easily twice what we need for dancing), so folks are welcome to come bring other SCA activities for the sidelines, or even to just come hang out! The site costs $100 per session; donations are optional, but welcome to help defray the cost of renting the hall. So come join us! It’s very much “the more, the merrier”, and you’re very welcome to join in!

description: Event details Rusted Woodlands is proud to once again announce we are hosting EK Novice Day 2026. Come and celebrate the accomplishments of our newest members in the East Kingdom’s Novice Day 2026. This event’s purpose is to celebrate our fledgling members into our community and give them a chance to showcase the talents they have developed in their inception to the SCA (within 2 years of their initial authorizations). We will have TWO (2) tournaments: * Armored Combat Tourney * Fencing Tournament All fighters please note: The tourneys will be preceded by a procession of the combatants with their consorts/inspirations. If a contestant doesn't have one, one will be provided. New Combatants will be able to authorize the day of the event. * There will also be archery and thrown weapons. * Sunshades and tents are allowed around the perimeter of the field. Due to the site's sprinkler system, stakes are not allowed beyond this area. The Arts and Sciences (A&S) remain an ever important and integral part of our Society and will be represented with their own competition. The A&S Competition is open to all gentles who hold neither a Kingdom or Baronial level A&S award, nor have ever won a major championship. The winner(s) will be decided by votes cast by both the Populace and the Laurels. ****SCHEDULE ADVISORY**** The schedule may be altered in the case of extreme heat or thunderstorms. Be prepared to be flexible, and don't forget to bring water. In case of rain, fencing will be moved into the covered pavilion. Tables will need to be moved to accommodate. . . . . . Fencing The champion of the East Kingdom Novice Day Fencing Tournament will earn a fancy scroll and the right to carry the Arma Novitii, which consists of the Champion’s Rapier, Buckler, and Baldric, for the time until the the next champion of Novice Day can be discovered. Your initial authorization must have been within two years of the date of the tournament (7/18/24 - 7/18/26). Fencers with AoA level awards ARE allowed to compete. Fencing Schedule and Rules: * This tournament is open to all fighters first authorized from 7/18/24 - 7/18/26). * Fencers with AoA level awards ARE allowed to compete. * Authorizations 10am-11am followed by procession of the novices (please check in with the MOL prior to the procession). Authorizations will end at 11am to allow for the procession to occur. * For fencers who are active MiTs, please let us know! You can help with authorizations in the morning and help marshal the melee games. * For any additional inquiries, please reach out to Percival Michaelson, or his deputy MiC, Serilda die Stollen * Tournament Starts immediately following the procession. * Tournament format: Round Robin - bring your best (spears are disallowed for this tournament). * Reduced armor will be permitted for the main tournament if you have signed up for the reduced armor experiment. * Melee games will be held following the tournament and are open to all fencers of any rank. We encourage any OGRs or MODs at the event to bring their gear to join in for the fun with the newest members of our family. ARMORED COMBAT Schedule: * Authorizations 10am-11am followed by procession of the novices (please check in with the MOL prior to the procession). Authorizations will end at 11am to allow for the procession to occur. * Tournament Starts at approximately 12pm Noon * This tournament is open to all fighters authorized for two (2) years or less. * Tournament format: round robin - bring your best (spears are disallowed for this tournament). * Classes will be held following the tournament. Classes are open to all attendees, not just those competing. . . . . . description: Hark! A Proclamation from the Sylvan Kingdom of Æthelmearc! To all brave knights, fencers of skill, artisans of renown, and good gentle folk, Hear ye, hear ye! The Upstate Renaissance Faire, held upon the grounds of Chenango in the town of Norwich, hath sent forth a royal request. Having missed the presence of honored historical reenactors, they invite the Society for Creative Anachronism to return for their 4th Annual gathering on August 29th & 30th, 2026. The Call to Arms: We summon the Heavies to take the field, the Rapier fighters to demonstrate the art of fence, and the Cut & Thrust champions to show their skill. Have your flattery and wit at the ready! - Scenario: Single Elimination, 1 Spicy Complement = 1 Extra Life Bonus - Spicy Compliment Bonus: 1 Per Tournament IMPORTANT: In order to earn the Extra Life Bonus, you must issue your compliment *prior* to exiting the field following a loss. description: Once a year, the veil between worlds grows thin, and ancient roads, long lost to time, reveal themselves once more. In the hidden places of history—where mysticism, superstition, and the macabre ruled the Middle Ages—a crossroads took root, forged by those who walked the forgotten paths of the thinning veil. Here, at the confluence of worlds, lies a place where treasures are exchanged, memories are honored, and history breathes. As the newly born Mourning Moon ascends, the pathways are open to this archaic place for all to journey. Beyond this threshold, wanderers and traders from the medieval world converge. You may find yourself learning arts long lost to time, trading tokens from another realm, unearthing forgotten tales by firelight, or discovering the rituals of undiscovered lands. title: Potted Arms and Fancy Faire: Summer In Bloom ***Now with FENCING TOURNEY DETAILS***
location: Unitarian Universalist Fellowship of Huntington 109 Browns Road Huntington, NY 11743 US
description: Join the Canton of Hawke’s Reache for our annual event, “Potted” Arms and Fancy “Faire”: Summer in Bloom! Spring has flowered into summer and Baronesses Fiona and Hugoline sojourn across the lands of An Dubhaigeainn to collect their tithes on the way to the Pennsic War. The Canton of Hawkes Reache welcomes one and all to a Summer Faire complete with a Tournament to select the new Baronial Fencing Champion. There will be a Hearty Dayboard served throughout the day. This years theme is an Exploration of Native Plants and Flowers. The menu includes Floral Centric delectables, and we ask the Fencers to Incorporate some form of Flora on their Hat… eschew those feathers for flowers!! No feast will be served but fear not, for no one leaves An Dubhaigeainn hungry! Once again we will conduct our endearingly lively Hat Auction, wherein the Populace bids on a Fencer as represented by their Hat. Auction proceeds benefit the Canton of Hawkes Reache. The victorious Hat Tournament Rapier Fighter, and their Generous Bidder, each will receive Wonderful Prizes! Auction is payable by cash or check only, no credit card payments for Fundraisers. The Baronial Fencing Tournament helps Their Excellencies Choose the next Baronial Rapier Champion – give Them your best Demonstration of Prowess, Courtesy, and Pageantry. The format has been set by Current Baronial Fencing Champion, Demetrio Antelini da Lucca. Demetrio, the current Baronial Fencing Champion, cut his teeth on the streets of his home city of Lucca, and to honor that legacy we're taking the fight to the streets of Hawkes Reach. Fighters will take to the alleys and junctions of the canton, all weapons drawn from the hip on the call of Lay On. Off-hand parry devices are welcome at the fighter's discretion, canes, torches, frying pans, whatever a street brawler might have on hand, though they are not treated as weapons. A quick wit and a sharp tongue are equally encouraged. Stage 1 is a team affair. Fighters will be grouped into teams of varying sizes and fight a series of bouts through the alleys, earning points not just for individual performance but for their ability to work together, protect their companions, and outlast their rivals. Those points will seed a Final 4 bracket, with the top seed facing the fourth and the second facing the third in the semifinals. Stage 2 is where the streets give way to the dueling ground. The two semifinal winners will meet in a Championship Finals fought as a best of 7, designed to test the full depth of a fencer's individual ability across multiple weapons forms. The Coronet selects the opening form, and from there the loser of each bout chooses what comes next, rewarding not just skill but versatility and adaptability. The fighter who prevails will be named the new Baronial Fencing Champion. All may enter; but only a Duck may Serve as Champion. Each entrant to the Baronial Tournament must have their Introduction to the List written out for a Herald to read. Entrants are strongly encouraged to bring their own over-the-top Herald (like in “A Knight’s Tale”). There will be a Prize and Recognition for best Heraldic Boast Performance! Come One, Come All to the Second Annual Baronial DUCK-OFF... Display your Quacking Best for Fun, Prizes, and Quacking Rights for a Year and a Day! Bring your Chairs and Blankets, take Respite upon the Lawns, Watch the Fencing and Play Silly Games. Merchants are most welcome to help us get in fine shopping form for Pennsic! Please contact the Event Steward to register as a merchant. Additional activities will be announced as they are confirmed. Event Schedule: 10:00 Site Opens 10:30 Morning Court 11:00 Fencing List Opens for inspections and authorisations 12:00 Day Board is served 12:30 Baronial Rapier Championship 2:00 Quack Off! 2:30 Hat Auction 3:00 Hat Tournament 4:00 Evening Court 6:00 Site Closes Site Opens: 10:00 AM Site Closes: 6:00 PM

description: Hosted by: Kaarnemaa | EN/FI/SWE Rajataverna - Gränstavernan 30.7-2.8.2026 Again, the northern medieval and Iron Age folk will gather on the border and welcome all travelers from near and far! This will be the first time the Tavern will be located in Finland. The site is a hunting lodge 10 km from the Swedish border. The event will be a relaxed reenactment event, which is open to new and old historical reenactors. The event is organized by the Peräpohjolan keskiaikaseura which is part of the international Society for Creative Anachronism and Suomen keskiaikaseura (The medieval society of Finland). In the terms of the Society: The village of Torna in Aarnimetsä, Drachenwald. We are even collaborating with Frostheim (Luleå) from the principality of Nordmark (Sweden) and are officially sponsored by Kaarnemaa (Oulu) from Aarnimetsä. Although Rajataverna / Gräsntavernan is a SCA-event, you do not need to be a member of the society in order to participate! Rajataverna is a place for everyone to meet regardless of any borders. The event languages are Finnish, Swedish and English. The program is currently under construction and we are looking for teachers in Arts & Sciences, fighting, etc. If you want to teach, let us know! There will be a homely feast and a small market, where you can bring new and second hand items. The program is updating all the time and the final schedule will be published well before the event. It is possible to arrive at the site on Friday 17 o’clock and the event site must be empty by midday on Sunday. Please note that Rajataverna is living in Finnish time due to its location. The hunting lodge Tapiolan maja has cabins for 24 persons. You are free to bring your own tent and we will create a crash space if needed. The lodge has a sauna and a fireplace. Whole weekend (includes accommodation & food) 40 € / 440 kr SCA-members 45 € / 470 kr non-members 20 € / 210 kr minors Children under 7 are free Day visit on Saturday (includes food) 15 € / 170 kr for an adult 10 € / 110 kr children over 7 years The meals include snacks on Friday evening, breakfast, lunch and feast on Saturday and breakfast on Sunday. People coming from outside the Nordics can pay at the door. Payment information will be sent later via email. Please note that the event is inclusive and we actively work towards a safe environment to have fun in. If you are interested, but new to reenactment, you can contact the event organizer for help. description: Royal Progress: Scarlet Guard Inn XI Shire of Hunters Home June 5, 2026, 3pm June 7, 2026, 1pm Fraternal Order of Eagles #965 1050 Eagle’s Nest Road Brockway PA 15824 Greetings archers and throwers! The Order of the Scarlet Guard and the Shire of Hunters Home invite you to attend the eleventh Scarlet Guard Inn Archery Festival. As with years past, there is a lot going on over this weekend, so here are the highlights! Archery! The main attraction is, of course, the archery. We can’t wait until Saturday to begin, so the annual Flight Shoot will be Friday evening. Saturday will see a smorgasbord of options, as we already have slated a bunch of novelty ranges, a couple woods walks, a clout range, and of course the Scarlet Guard Challenge. Speaking of which… The Scarlet Guard Challenge! Any group with a seneschal can send one archer as a representative, as long as the archer is not a member of the Scarlet Guard, equivalent, or higher Order. Anyone who has previously won the Scarlet Guard Challenge is likewise ineligible to compete again. Once a group has chosen their archer, please contact Master Juan Miguel Cezar () with the name of the group being represented, the name of the seneschal, and the name of the archer no later than June 3, 2026. For the tournament itself, archers MUST bring a letter signed by the seneschal declaring them as the chosen representative of that group, as well as a small prize to be added to a gift basket which will be presented to the winner along with the ancestral banner which bears the name of all past winners and the groups they have represented. Thrown Weapons! We already support the flinging of wood and metal through the air, regardless of its shape, but this year brings something special. It has been declared that the Aethelmearc Thrown Weapons Champion will be determined at the Scarlet Guard Inn! Throw for fun! Throw for glory! (Or both, both is good) Bardic! Come enjoy the camaraderie and entertainment of our bardic circle tradition. Whether it is under the roof of the big pavilion or gathering around our large fire ring, each night everyone is encouraged to help fill the air with songs and stories. Merchants! Hunters Home invites merchants to set up their wares at no additional charge. We had many great items for sale at our last event. Please inform the autocrat so that we can reserve space for you. Camping! Camping is free! Please feel free to stay Friday and Saturday night. There is plenty of camping space. Some already have regular spots, but it IS first come first serve. There is space for RVs but it is limited and there are no hookups and no dumping allowed, please contact the autocrat ahead of time. We have a community campfire that everyone is welcome to join, but if you choose to have your own campfire that is fine as long as you leave the site as you found it. The Tavern! The Food: There will be no feast at this event, however there will be a modest sideboard open Friday evening and throughout the day on Saturday in the tavern. The Games: Want to compete off the range as well? Two gaming tables will be set aside in the tavern with an assortment of games to choose from. We welcome any additions. In addition to the bardic offerings, period games have proven to be a popular way to spend the evenings. Some general notes: -Your equipment will need to be inspected before engaging in martial activities, so please give yourself time to get inspected. -The site is discreetly wet. Just make sure you clean up any messes and leave the site as you found it. -Being June in Pennsylvania, and since this site isn’t conveniently close to any major shopping areas, be prepared for any weather. This means both sunscreen and some way to stay warm through the night. -Bug and tick spray! We had a good long freeze this winter, so maybe they won’t be as bad this year, but it’s better safe than sorry. The schedule as it currently stands: Friday 3pm Site Opens 7pm Flight Shoot Saturday 9am Troll Opens 10am Morning Court 10am – after court – All ranges open. 11am Qualifier for Thrown Weapons Championships begins 3pm Thrown Weapons Championships finals 345pm Ranges close 4pm Scarlet Guard Challenge 5pm Awards Ceremony and Royal Court Sunday 12pm Site Closes This schedule is subject to change Adult Event Registration is $30, Adult Member Discount Event Registration is $20, Children 6-17: $5, Children 5 and under: Free. Make checks payable to SCA-PA, Inc. – Shire of Hunters Home. Reservations may be sent to the Autocrat. description: Come celebrate the East Kingdom's oldest shire as we turn 50! This will be a Full weekend of events with a magical feast! We open Friday night with a potluck Tavern night with a hafla and music. Saturday we will have heavy fighting, fencing, archery, thrown weapons; Arts & Sciences classes & displays. Guild meetings for Blacksmiths, soothsayers, and foresters! Sunday we will have our usual Shire martial championships. We welcome Merchants to come sell their wares with no booth charge. We will be having an amazing feast Saturday night with culinary dishes from around the world and across times! Pre-reg is required to get on board for it. After Feast Saturday night, we will be having a Tudor/Elizabethan dessert board with dancing and revelry. description: For Twelfth Night 2027, the populace is invited to celebrate a season of transition, where old traditions and joyful excess meet at the turning of the year. The theme draws inspiration from late medieval southern Germany and Switzerland, where winter observances blended seamlessly with lively seasonal celebrations marking the close of one cycle and the promise of the next. By the fifteenth century, these celebrations had fused into a distinctive blend of formality and fun. Daytime brought courtly pomp, displays of skill, and structured ceremony, while nightfall ushered in feasting, dancing, and masked revelry. This balance of order and exuberance provides the perfect setting for Atlantia’s Twelfth Night, offering a full day of pageantry and arts followed by an evening devoted to celebration, community, and unapologetic joy. During this time, the days surrounding Twelfth Night marked the end of the winter holiday season and the gradual shift toward spring. Communities gathered for pageantry, symbolic acts of renewal, and public festivities that reflected both reflection and anticipation. These moments were as much about community and tradition as they were about marking time itself. Alongside this came Fasnacht, a vibrant pre Lenten carnival that preserved much older seasonal customs. Masquerades, mummers, and playful processions filled towns with music, laughter, and satire. Masks and costumes allowed for mischief and creativity, and the rules of everyday life were happily bent before the long quiet of late winter.

description: Let the word spread far and wide, Whipping Winds is upon us! There are rustlings north of the border!! A voice on the wind calls “we’re not dead yet, eh!” Travel to the Northern Realms for the last celebration of the summer season! Join the Shire of Windegate at Williamson Park in Shelby Montana and celebrate in jubilant Northern style as Hordes from Avacal cross the border once again to celebrate our friendship. We hope! Fighting, Archery, Thrown Weapons, Dancing and Music, Arts and Classes, and Shopping! All are to be found in abundant supply amongst the trees along the shore of the Marias River. Before we batten down the hatches for the long nights of winter, the Kingdoms of Artemisia and Avacal shall join together on the fields of battle, and around the campfires beneath the stars, to solidify our mutual respect and kinship. The Autocrat team is planning activities for full days of merriment and contests! There will be Armored battles, on the main field, and into the woods! Don’t forget our Founder's Battle, and Sir Terrell’s booty tournament. Rapier will also have battle scenes and tournaments to determine who is the best. For the Arts & Sciences minded persons, we are planning to have classes, and display for your projects. Archery is a mainstay at this event, and there will be animal targets, Royal Rounds, and three archery championships. The site is south of Shelby Montana, on the Marias River. At this time of year, the Marias is a wonderfully slow-moving river that has room for wading & swimming. Parents are asked to keep a mindful eye on their children. There are shade trees, an area for RV’s, a permanent playground, and a permanent building for toilets & fresh water. Fire restrictions will be dependent on Seasonal USFS restrictions. Pets allowed, on leash. FEES: Adults {age 18 years +} event registration fee for the weekend: $35.00 USD. Our site is shaded with grass and trees and has a large building we will use for court, classes, and revelry. Above-ground fire pits are welcomed.
